place.description:
Jerusalem, called the “great city” and the capital of the kingdom of [Judah|judah], is the place from which the record opens. {Lehi|lehi1} had dwelt there all his days when, in the first year of the reign of {Zedekiah|zedekiah1} king of [Judah|judah] (about 600 BC), many prophets came warning the people that they must repent or the city would be destroyed. {Lehi|lehi1} was among them, and he was commanded by {God|god} to take his family and flee (1 Nephi 1:4).

{Lehi|lehi1}’s departure became the record’s timeline marker: six hundred years from the time he left Jerusalem, {the Lord|jesus-christ} would raise up a {Messiah|jesus-christ}, a {Savior|jesus-christ} of the world, among {the Jews|jews} (1 Nephi 10:4). In vision, {Nephi|nephi1} saw the great city of Jerusalem and other cities, including [Nazareth|nazareth], where he beheld the virgin who would be the mother of {the Son of God|jesus-christ} (1 Nephi 11:13). {Nephi|nephi1} wrote of his own anguish of spirit for those who remained at Jerusalem, whom {the Lord|jesus-christ} had shown him would otherwise have perished (1 Nephi 19:20).

{Lehi|lehi1} told his sons he had seen a vision in which he knew Jerusalem was destroyed, and that had they stayed they too would have died (2 Nephi 1:4). {Nephi|nephi1} recorded the prophecy that those at Jerusalem would crucify {the God of Israel|jesus-christ} and be scourged by all people for it (1 Nephi 19:13), and that though the people were carried away, they would return and again possess the land of Jerusalem, their land of inheritance (2 Nephi 25:11).

The record also preserves an eschatological distinction about Jerusalem’s ultimate fate. {Moroni|moroni2}, abridging the vision of {Ether|ether}, records that the Jerusalem from which {Lehi|lehi1} came would, after its destruction, be built up again as a holy city of {the Lord|jesus-christ} — yet it could not be the New Jerusalem, for it was already ancient; a separate New Jerusalem would be built on the American continent for the remnant of the seed of {Joseph|joseph1} (Ether 13:5–6).
